title: The Procession Beacon
logline: A religious cantor discovers the sacred parade lantern houses a century-old audio flight recorder exposing a suppressed colonial atrocity before the annual holy broadcast.

roles.description: Guides ceremonial shuttle flight paths; devout, burdened by conscience, terrified that holy ritual is built upon a massacre.
Municipal historical commissioner; smooth, dismissive, determined to keep colonial records sanitized.
A council gunboat tasked with jamming unauthorized broadcast signals along the parade route.
Independent mining families who pilot small shuttles in close formation for annual blessings.
The ruling municipal authority, protective of its founding pedigree and security legacy.
An ancient domed temple station overlooking the primary mineral belt.
The high-gain transmitter mast atop the civic hub used for holiday feeds.
A sealed records depository in the station core housing sealed colonial registries.

public_situation: Thousands gather at {role:lantern_sanctuary} for the lighting of the great relic lantern, which broadcasts founding hymns across {system}.
private_truth: {role:procession_cantor} discovered the lantern's memory core holds raw black-box telemetry of station gunners firing on civilian shuttle pods during the Founding Riots.

beats.public_change: Pilgrim vessels power ceremonial amber running lights while {role:station_council} deploys monitoring probes along the approach corridor.

missions.reason: He needs an unmonitored pilot to carry the relic lantern's unsealed memory prism to the archive vault for independent sensor verification before opening prayers.
missions.private_fact: He matched the prism's acoustic serial code to an old military gun-camera log that was supposedly destroyed forty years ago.

beats.public_change: {role:station_council} announces unexpected data maintenance on the archive vault, barring civilian visitors from inspection terminals.

missions.reason: He needs an outside pilot to scan sealed registry backups and extract the voice encryption keys needed to verify the black-box recording.
missions.private_fact: The historical casualty register shows his own grandfather signed the execution order for the rebellious miners.

beats.public_change: {role:patrol_interceptor} takes position over {role:broadcast_spire}, scanning incoming ships for encrypted audio payloads.

missions.reason: He needs the council interceptor disabled so the transmission array at the broadcast spire remains open to external feeds.
missions.private_fact: The interceptor captain hails offering a council commission and immune status if the pilot burns the telemetry prism.

beats.public_change: The ceremonial procession moves into formation as opening choral fanfares echo across station frequencies.

missions.reason: He asks the pilot to deliver the unlocked memory prism to the transmitter controls at the broadcast spire before the holiday service concludes.
missions.private_fact: He intends to override the master acoustic feed with the un-redacted gunner recording and announce his own immediate resignation.

player_choice.prompt: The pilot holds the verified black-box telemetry at the broadcast spire controls while opening choral anthems ring across the system.

options.label: Transmit the massacre telemetry over live festival feeds
Hand the prism to the cantor to seal within the high altar
Sell the telemetry to the archivist for council hush money

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot disables the interceptor and transmits the black-box data.
resolutions.summary: The black-box telemetry airs over every festival feed. Outrage erupts across {system}, council leaders face widespread protests, and the holy celebration turns into a general strike.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot plugged fifty-year-old gun-camera logs into a holiday transmitter and broke the council's sacred myth.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot returns the prism to the cantor to be sealed in the shrine.
resolutions.summary: {role:procession_cantor} locks the memory core inside the sealed high altar. The founding hymns play on schedule, but the clergy quietly extracts political concessions from {role:station_council}.

consequences.public_summary: Whispers say the temple elders bought their new tax exemptions with an unexploded piece of colonial history.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot sells the telemetry to municipal censors or takes the interceptor's bribe.
resolutions.summary: The telemetry core is surrendered to municipal censors. {role:station_council} destroys the evidence, pays off the participants, and broadcasts sanitized holiday anthems.

consequences.public_summary: Dockside gossip claims an independent pilot took council gold to make sure an old colony scandal stayed dead.

resolutions.reached_by: The archive verification fails or the pilot abandons the contract.
resolutions.summary: Security sweeps seize the ceremonial reliquary before the truth leaks. The holiday hymns play on schedule while {role:procession_cantor} is quietly reassigned to an unpopulated ice outpost.

loose_threads.detail: A decommissioned militia tactical channel briefly transmits handshake tones whenever the temple choir sings the fifth stanza.
The temple sanctuary auxiliary power budget is encumbered by an old debt bond held by a council member's holding trust.
The archive access certificate on the registry terminal bears the digital seal of an inspector who died twelve years ago.

radio_hooks: Pilgrim shuttle formations tune transmitter horns across {system} for evening blessing.
Station council announces enhanced telemetry monitoring along the procession axis.
Historical commission reminds citizens that founding archive maintenance is routine.

voice_direction.procession_cantor: Speaks with soft, lyrical cadences that hesitate whenever historical casualty dates are mentioned. Avoids administrative terms entirely.
voice_direction.station_archivist: Smooth, clipped, and relentlessly cheerful. Dismisses questions about early colonial gunnery as unhelpful historical gossip.
